Themarenn (A95)

Scoring-table region: Empire of Anbennar (EoA).

In brief: A small duchy of river raiders' descendants turns the Esmar River into the foundation of a diplomatic principality, rebuilding Esmaria through canals, sailors, and relations among the princes.

Narrative: medium-high | Mission tree: medium (37 direct missions) | Mission-tree update: exact date unverified; local version v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: high | Tedium: medium | Early pressure: medium | Expansion capacity: medium-high.

A Small River State, Not Merely a Passing Prince

Themarenn already exists in 1444: it is an Esmari-culture monarchy of the Regent Court, with its capital by the Esmar River. The current in-game localization and the legacy scoring-table queue use different Chinese renderings of its name; both refer to the same Tag. This English text uses the native name Themarenn. It is not a Tag formed by another country, and its unique decision serves its own river and manpower systems. 【Local history script】【Local localization】

The English offline Wiki's country entry offers only a short overview, so it cannot support an invented dynastic chronicle; the related character entry provides a firmer account of its origins. In 1006, the Black Castanorian warlord Drosten switched sides from his former masters to the League of Free Realms, but after the war refused to return his lands along the Esmar River. He maintained his rule with his army and an elite guard skilled in river warfare. He is described as an ancestor of the modern Themarenn house. This history helps explain the country's dual character as both an imperial-border nobility and river warriors, but does not directly establish every detail of its 1444 government. 【Wiki】

Another historical backdrop is the long entanglement of Esmari nobles and valley politics. A related Wiki biography records how a marriage dispute and war around 1270 changed Konwell's independence. This is regional context; it does not establish that Themarenn already held its future mission objectives in 1444. The country's appeal lies in that contrast: a small duchy bearing a river-raider reputation seeks to redefine itself through canals, diplomacy, and administrative capacity. 【Wiki】【Local script】

From River Raiders to an Esmari Diplomatic Center

The 37 direct missions broadly organize the campaign around three connected directions. First are riverways and naval manpower: missions develop inland canals and impressment offices, strengthening sailor supplies. A unique decision can switch between noble levies and Themarenn sailor privileges, subject to a loyalty threshold. This is more than a numerical reward; it makes the military organization of an inland river state part of the gameplay. Noble land forces and professional river personnel are distinct resources. 【Local script】

The second direction is Esmari diplomatic integration. Later missions emphasize relations, subjects, imperial interaction, and treaties, aiming to restore regional order rather than simply conquer to the edge of the map. The player still has to manage territory and political standing, but “restoring the duchy” in the missions must not be rewritten as something already accomplished in 1444. Official Dev Diary #71 listed restoration of the duchy as a direction for Themarenn's rework; the current base-game missions show that this direction has been implemented, while the diary itself does not prove every current-version condition. 【Local script】【Official Dev Diary】

The third direction is religious and dynastic choice. Missions centered on Ryala and Esmaryal branch according to personal deities and regional control. Events involving administrative burdens and an heir's prosperity give “reconstruction” a cost of governance. The player may pursue a more distinct local faith and royal narrative, but the branches are not all inevitable endings at once. This is a mission tree that ties local traditions, imperial politics, and state administration together, suited to players who like diplomacy with concrete mechanics. 【Local script】【Local narrative text】

Gameplay, Personality, and Recommendation

Themarenn is not a completely peaceful diplomatic campaign. You still need to hold the river line, secure the appropriate core region, and manage noble loyalty and sailor supplies; then use relations, subjects, and imperial politics to turn these resources into regional influence. Player posts often recommend it to those who enjoy diplomatic prestige, river raiders, and marines, but these are subjective experiences from particular periods, not evidence for current-version values or an “optimal opening.” 【Local script】【Community opinion】

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansionism 66/100 | Authoritarianism 57/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 61/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 43/100) | Pluralism 72/100.

The v2.1 values score is Neutral (66/100), with a mixed trajectory.

Recommended for players who want to shape their realm through diplomacy, riverine commerce, and dynastic storytelling. It may feel circuitous if you want pure military snowballing or dislike religious, noble, and relationship requirements in missions. Source levels and branch boundaries are documented on the evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Themarennic Traditions

  • Land leader maneuver: +1 (leader_land_manuever; raw value 1).

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

1. Hub of Esmaria

The beautiful shores of the Themarenn Lake have always been a popular destination for wanderers in Esmaria, in the old days of the Kingdom of Esmaria it was even the preferred location for the King's residence, with the various river kings making the travel between Esmarainé and Lake Themarenn several times. Ever since the death of the last King of Esmaria, with Esmarainé fallen to the hands of greedy merchants, the Lake has assumed the role of Hub of Esmaria.

  • Diplomats: +1 (diplomats; raw value 1).

2. Mastery of the Riverways

Esmaria is well known for its many rivers, most of which are tributaries of the Esmar River. The river kings were able to use them to connect the region and establish reliable borders for their vassals. Due to the constant stream of visitors, we have been forced to make the most out of the old waterways, resulting in our exceptional ability in navigating them.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. Defenders of the Lake

The beautiful shores of the lake attract many visitors. Most of them just come to enjoy the scenery and the fair maidens on its shores, while some come with more hostile intentions. As tensions in the region rise, it is time we finally take up arms to defend our home!

  • Land force limit modifier: +15% (land_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.15).

4. River-Reaver Marines

Seen by their neighbours as no more than brutes who can swim, the River-Reaver Marines gain their name from the renowned Black Castanorian commander Drosten River-Reaver who first occupied Themarenn and much of the central Esmar river for the Sorcerer-King. When the war turned sour he quickly joined the side of the League of Free Realms in 1006, and used his skill in river-fighting to help liberate the rest of Esmaria and push into Escann via the Alen river. After the war he was ordered to give the lands he occupied with his army back to the Esmarians but he refused, and used his River-Reavers to continue to dominate the riverways of the Esmar against his foes. Despite this, thanks to his companionship with the elf Saelihn he was a major force in the elvenization of the region.

  • shock_damage_received：-10% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

  • Marine force limit: +25% (allowed_marine_fraction; raw value 0.25).

5. Floating Fortresses

Besieging a fortress is hard. Besieging a coastal fortress is even harder without a fleet. Besieging a fortress completely surrounded by deep water might as well be impossible. Although we aren't able to build stone keeps on water, by constructing small wooden keeps on water that are able to house a few cannons the would-be conquerors will have many difficulties in bringing down our fortresses.

  • Fort defense: +15% (defensiveness; raw value 0.15).

6. Lake Themarenn Feasts

The Esmari River Parties are famed in all of Cannor. What reaches even the neighbouring regions, from the rebuilt Escann to the far lands of Bulwar, are the feasts by Lake Themarenn. By improving our infrastructure, we will be able to host more guests, and to separate the illustrious ones from the peasants.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

7. Themarenn Palace

The Esmarian Kings routinely retreated from the busy court life in Esmarainé to find peace in their palace by the lake. The Lake Palace was left in a state of disrepair ever since the river kings died out, due to its high maintenance cost. But now, as we possess the funds to rebuild and maintain such a splendid palace, we shall show to the whole of Esmaria our great power and wealth.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).
